import { Blocks, FileCode, FlaskConical, Search, Terminal, TriangleAlert } from 'lucide-react';

Use this checklist before you deploy or upgrade a program on Gorbagana.

<Callout type="warn" title="This is not an audit">
  This checklist helps catch common SVM and Anchor mistakes. It does not replace a security review for programs that hold meaningful value.
</Callout>

## Before you deploy

Complete these checks before a live deploy or upgrade.

- Run local tests and review failing paths, not only happy paths.
- Run a small live smoke test only after local tests pass.
- Check that clients use the correct Program ID.
- Check the upgrade authority keypair and custody plan.
- Inspect the deployed program with `solana program show` after every deploy or upgrade.

## Account validation

Validate every account your instruction depends on.

| Check | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| Owner | Prevents a caller from passing an account controlled by the wrong program |
| Account type | Confirms the account data matches the struct or discriminator you expect |
| Executable flag | Confirms program accounts are executable when you expect a program |
| Address | Confirms hard-coded or derived addresses match the intended account |
| Data length | Prevents reads or writes against accounts with unexpected layout |
| Initialization state | Prevents re-initialization or use of uninitialized data |

For Anchor, use constraints such as `owner`, `address`, `has_one`, `seeds`, `bump`, `mut`, and typed account wrappers where they fit the instruction.

## Signer and writable checks

Keep signer and writable requirements explicit.

- Require `Signer` only for accounts that must authorize the instruction.
- Mark accounts writable only when the instruction changes lamports or data.
- Check that the expected authority signs the instruction.
- Watch for duplicate mutable accounts when two account fields must be different.
- Do not assume the fee payer is also the program authority.

Anchor constraints can express many of these checks, but you still need to decide which account should have each privilege.

## PDA checks

Program Derived Addresses should be deterministic and checked with the same seeds your program uses.

- Use stable seeds.
- Use the canonical bump unless your design requires another value.
- Check the PDA belongs to the expected program.
- Recreate signer seeds carefully before CPI calls.
- Check authority assumptions when a PDA signs for token transfers, account closes, or state changes.

Example Anchor shape:

```rust
#[account(
    seeds = [b"vault", authority.key().as_ref()],
    bump,
)]
pub vault: SystemAccount<'info>,
```

## Token checks

Token instructions need more checks than a native GOR transfer.

| Check | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| Mint | Confirms the instruction uses the intended token |
| Token account owner | Confirms the token account belongs to the expected authority |
| Token program | Confirms the instruction calls the intended token program |
| Associated token account | Confirms wallet, mint, and token program match the expected ATA |
| Decimals | Prevents UI and base-unit conversion mistakes |
| Transfer authority | Confirms the signer or PDA can move the tokens |
| Balance delta | Confirms the instruction changed balances by the intended amount |

Use native GOR for fees and deployments on Gorbagana. Use the bridge docs when your flow moves between Solana GOR and native GOR.

## CPI checks

Cross-program invocations pass account privileges to another program. Review them carefully.

- Check the target program ID.
- Check account order and account mutability.
- Limit `remaining_accounts` to what the instruction actually needs.
- Review signer privilege forwarding.
- Recreate PDA signer seeds from trusted state, not unchecked user input.
- Check return values or post-conditions when the called program can fail or produce partial state.

## State and math checks

Review every state transition.

- Check overflow and underflow.
- Check rounding and base-unit conversions.
- Make initialization idempotent or explicitly one-time.
- Prevent replay when an instruction should run once.
- Check close behavior and destination accounts.
- Check rent and balance assumptions.
- Store enough state to verify future instructions.

## Upgrade lifecycle

Program authority is part of the security model.

| Decision | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Deploy | Save Program ID and deployment signature |
| Inspect | Run `solana program show PROGRAM_ID` and check ProgramData, authority, data length, and balance |
| Upgrade | Confirm the current authority is expected and the new binary is intentional |
| Transfer authority | Confirm the new authority keypair or governance account is controlled |
| Make immutable | Confirm the program should never be updated or closed |
| Close | Confirm the Program ID no longer needs to be used |

<Callout type="warn" title="Immutable and close are permanent decisions">
  Removing upgrade authority prevents future updates. Closing a program prevents reuse of that Program ID.
</Callout>

## Final review

Before you call the program from a user-facing app, confirm:

- local tests passed
- a small live smoke test passed
- the client uses the intended Program ID
- `solana program show` matches the expected ProgramData and authority
- the explorer shows the deploy or upgrade signature
- account constraints match the instruction design
- token and PDA authority paths are covered by tests
- upgrade authority custody is documented for the project
